Pope Pius VII, who had been Napoleon's prisoner, regained the Papal States; at the congress his interests were defended by Cardinal Ercole Consalvi. In 1815 Murat moved against Austria, called on the Italians to unite and was defeated; that autumn he was shot in Calabria. Ferdinand returned and in 1816 united Naples and Sicily into the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, and under a secret treaty with Austria undertook not to introduce a constitution. Italy did not become an «Austrian province», but Vienna gained decisive influence over the peninsula. Later, in 1847, Metternich would write: «Italy is merely a geographical expression.»
level.vienna_1815.goal: The Congress of Vienna redraws the peninsula: Austria takes the north, Savoy gets Genoa, the pope returns to Rome, and a Bourbon unites Naples and Sicily
level.vienna_1815.hint: Metternich builds his order in the south after securing the north. Promises of liberty have no place in that order.
level.vienna_1815.intro: 1814–1815. Napoleon has fallen, and in Vienna monarchs and diplomats are deciding Europe's fate. In Italy there are many questions: who gets Lombardy and the former Venetian Republic, will the pope return, what to do with Genoa, and who will rule Naples — the Bourbon Ferdinand, who fled to Sicily, or Napoleon's marshal Joachim Murat, who went over to Austria in 1814. The chief architect of the new order is the Austrian foreign minister Klemens von Metternich.
level.vienna_1815.source: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna (9 June 1815); Klemens von Metternich, «Memoirs»
level.vienna_1815.title: Italy, a Geographical Expression
level.vittorio_1918.fact: On 16 October 1918 Charles I issued the manifesto «To My Loyal Peoples», promising to turn Austria into a federation — but national councils were already proclaiming independence. On 24 October, the anniversary of Caporetto, Diaz launched his offensive; on 30 October the Italians entered Vittorio Veneto, while Austro-Hungarian units refused to fight and went home. On 3 November at Villa Giusti near Padua, General Viktor Weber von Webenau signed the armistice; the Italian delegation was headed by General Pietro Badoglio. The guns fell silent on 4 November at 3 p.m.; owing to confusion over the time the Austrians stopped earlier, and in the last day hundreds of thousands of soldiers were taken prisoner. Diaz announced the victory in the «Victory Bulletin». Italy paid for the war with some 650,000 soldiers dead, and the disputes over the peace of 1919 are another story.
level.vittorio_1918.goal: As Austria-Hungary breaks apart along national lines, Diaz crosses the Piave — and at Villa Giusti the empire signs an armistice
level.vittorio_1918.hint: Diaz waited until autumn. The empire was collapsing from within — but the armistice still had to be sanctioned by the emperor.
level.vittorio_1918.intro: Summer 1918. The Austro-Hungarian offensive on the Piave has failed. The Allies urge General Armando Diaz: attack! But Diaz waits — after Caporetto the army cannot afford a second disaster. And in Vienna the young Emperor Charles I watches his multinational empire crack: Czechs, South Slavs, Poles and Hungarians are preparing states of their own.
level.vittorio_1918.source: Armistice of Villa Giusti (3 November 1918); Armando Diaz, Bollettino della Vittoria (4 November 1918)
level.vittorio_1918.title: Vittorio Veneto
level.young_italy_1831.fact: At the last moment the Duke of Modena betrayed Menotti: he was arrested and in 1831 hanged. The risings in Modena, Parma and the Papal States were crushed by the Austrians. Mazzini drew his conclusion: secret societies, with their rituals and their hopes in princes, were doomed. In Marseille he founded «Young Italy» — a secret revolutionary organization with an openly proclaimed programme and a clear goal: a united, independent, republican Italy, liberated by the people themselves. He did nonetheless write an open letter to Charles Albert calling on him to lead the cause — and in reply received an order for his arrest. In 1833 a sailor from Nice, Giuseppe Garibaldi, joined the society. In 1834 he was to raise the fleet in Genoa, but the plot was uncovered; Garibaldi was sentenced to death in absentia and fled to South America. Mazzini's risings almost always failed, but he created the language of national politics that the whole Risorgimento spoke.
level.young_italy_1831.goal: After the Carbonari plots fail, the exile Mazzini founds «Young Italy» — and among its first members is a young sailor, Garibaldi, who will soon be sentenced to death
level.young_italy_1831.hint: Wait for neither dukes nor kings. Whoever stands beside a trusting conspirator will share his fate.
level.young_italy_1831.intro: 1831. In Modena, Ciro Menotti is preparing a rising and pins his hopes on the duke himself, Francis IV, who supposedly dreams of an Italian crown. In Piedmont, Charles Albert ascends the throne — the very prince who in 1821 granted a constitution and promptly abandoned it. A young Genoese lawyer, Giuseppe Mazzini, who has already done time in the fortress of Savona for links with the Carbonari, is exiled from the country.
level.young_italy_1831.source: Giuseppe Mazzini, «The Duties of Man» (1860); Giuseppe Garibaldi, «Memoirs»
level.young_italy_1831.title: Young Italy
